messages:
Evan: Large enterprise prospect - must retain root keys in their HSM, monthly rotation, and require HSM attestations. They're asking if Redwood can integrate with on-prem KMIP gateways for hosted API. POC next Monday.
Nina: We support KMIP and cloud KMS integrations. For on-prem KMIP we'll need either a reachable endpoint or a VPN/VPC peering. If they want us to talk to a gateway in their network, that typically adds 2-3 weeks.
Ravi: Technical details: Redwood uses envelope encryption. Flow: customer CMK (HSM) wraps data keys; Redwood never has plaintext CMK. We cache encrypted data keys at runtime; cache TTL is configurable. Rotation is supported via detection of new key versions and atomic promotion.
Evan: Customer also asked about importing wrapped keys vs. remote key usage. Which is supported?
Nina: Both. If they can export wrapped key material we can import a wrapped key into our key store (still HSM protected). Preferred is remote WKU (wrap/unwrap remotely) so customer custody stays in their HSM.
Ravi: For attestation: CloudHSM provides FIPS/attestation PDFs. For Thales/others we'll request vendor attestation. If customer needs remote attestation (TPM-style), we should confirm vendor support; not all HSMs expose that.
Evan: Pricing ask: customer wants BYOK on hosted API. Sales wants a concise pricing line for the SOW. Nina any suggestion?
Nina: Suggest: BYOK add-on $750/mo + one-time integration fee $3k for KMIP/VPN setup; if dedicated network (private peering) charge as infra uplift by project. Add a per-POC engineering day rate if they want heavy load testing.
Ravi: POC checklist (short):
- Exchange KMIP endpoint or KMS ARN + access principal
- Share attestation certs
- Link key alias in Redwood console and run encrypt/decrypt smoke tests
- Run load test (50-200 TPS) and capture P95/P99 latency
- Execute scheduled rotation and validate no downtime
Example command: `redwood keys link --alias corp-hsm --endpoint \"kmip://203.0.113.10:5696\"`
Evan: Security questionnaire draft answer: \"Redwood never exports customer master key material. Envelope encryption is used; key operations are logged and can be exported to customer's SIEM.\" Add note about key deletion workflow?
Ravi: Add: \"Key deletion is gated and logged; Redwood requires written deletion requests and can provide deletion receipts.\"
Evan: Legal: we need a BYOK addendum for key custody, liability, and attestation acceptance. @LegalBot can you provide standard wording?
LegalBot: Uploaded a BYOK addendum template to the deal workspace. Highlights: custody, audit logs, key deletion process, liability cap, and acceptance of vendor attestations. Recommend redline for customer-specific attestation requirements.
OpsBot: POC infra created: redwood-byo-poc-1782267890. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/poc/1782267890. Network note: if endpoint is private, request a VPN termination IP to allow KMIP traffic.
Nina: I'll coordinate the runbook and sec-q answers. Evan I'll draft the SOW line items and attach to the invite.
Evan: Customer call Monday 10am PT. Agenda: confirm attestation docs, confirm reachable KMIP endpoint, agree on pricing and SOW, finalize POC success criteria.
